thread:
mira: quick check — onboarding aurora-21b. weights are at s3://redwood-models/aurora/21b/v1/ (sha: 9f3a7c). uploaded yesterday, but tokenizer mapping looks off in the test harness.
mira: when I run a sample inference I see broken eos handling (generated continuing text) — suspect tokenizer.eos_token_id differs from model config.
sam_g: noted. did we convert with the new tokenizer pipeline (tokenize_v2)? sometimes `bos/eos` rename slips. which tokenizer file is in the bundle?
mira: bundle contains tokenizer.json + merges.v2. tokenizer.json has "eos_token": "</s>" but the model config uses eos_id: 1. quick dump: `jq .eos_token_id model-config.json` -> 2
alex: that mismatch explains it. either remap ids or update model-config.json to eos 2. remapping is safer for now.
mira: I pushed a small helper in the PR that rewrites ids during load if a mapping exists: https://github.com/redwood-inference/models/pull/842 — last commit adds a warning log.
jlee: quick question re serving config: what are we using for continuous batching and KV prefetch? metrics for aurora 21b show tail p50 rising when batch_window_ms > 10.
sam_g: current canary config I used is below:
```yaml
model: aurora-21b
continuous_batching:
  enabled: true
  batch_window_ms: 12
  max_batch_tokens: 8192
  max_batch_size: 32
cache:
  policy: prefix
  kv_prefetch: true
  kv_prefetch_workers: 4
  kv_cache_ttl_ms: 600000
scheduler:
  algo: fairshare
  prefetch_ratio: 0.25
limits:
  max_tokens_per_request: 4096
```
sam_g: this was tuned for throughput; latency-sensitive routes need lower `max_tokens_per_request`.
mira: noted — for our internal smoke tests I lowered to 2048. also reduced `max_batch_tokens` to 4096 and batch_window_ms to 8 in the branch.
infra-bot: deploy pipeline started for pr-842 — build 6281. logs: https://ci.redwood.ai/builds/6281 (watch) :building_construction:
onboard-bot: smoke tests queued on canary node rguard-12 (GPU A100x2). test suite: models/smoke/aurora-21b.yaml
jlee: can we also enable prefix cache warmup for common prompts used in eval set? that should reduce token generation early penalties.
sam_g: yes — I added a `cache.warmup_prompts` list in the PR. example: ["Summarize:", "Explain like I'm 5:"]
mira: small gotcha: tokenizer merges.v2 contains an unexpected `@@` token that the runtime treats as continuation marker and it's inflating token counts in the scheduler.
alex: we should normalize merges during build. add a sanitize step in packaging: `scripts/tokenizer_sanitize.py --strip-continuation`
sam_g: agreed. adding to PR now. also adding a test that asserts token_count(sample) < expected_threshold.
mira: smoke results are coming in — first run shows p50 210ms, p95 720ms (with modified config).
jlee: p95 is acceptable for canary but we should gate dedicated customers to max p95 600ms. set a canary alert.
alex: I'll add an alert rule in console: `aurora-21b-canary-p95 > 600ms for 5m -> rollback canary`.
mira: PR #842 has the packaging + config changes. can reviewers ping? @sam_g @alex @jlee please take a look.
sam_g: on it, will review tonight.
alex: reviewing now, leaving a small comment about reducing `kv_prefetch_workers` to 2 for A100 machines to avoid memory spikes.
infra-bot: build 6281 passed unit tests, started canary rollout to rguard-12.
onboard-bot: canary smoke passed (6/6 tests) on rguard-12.
mira: merging once approvals in. thanks all — will follow up with perf dashboard links and a tiny runbook for the tokenizer quirk. :tada:
